issue.title: Can we color issue labels to allow for grouping and reduce cognitive load?

labels.name: question
labels.description: This issue asks a question about ESLint

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
This has nothing to do with ESLint as an application, just a repository management concern.

I'd like to see if we could group some issue labels together and use the same color, to make it easier for us to learn how an issue is scoped. For example, "build"/"cli"/"infrastructure"/"core"/"rule" could be grouped as a sort of "scope" label group, and they could all be the same color; then if I see a label that's (for example) blue then I know it's for scope and will be one of those five values.

I tried to do that in my eslint-plugin-qunit repository (see [here](https://github.com/platinumazure/eslint-plugin-qunit/labels), don't know if the page is viewable without being a collaborator), but the label space is much simpler there since it is assumed that pretty much all issues have to do with a rule.

Synopsis of what I'm doing in eslint-plugin-qunit:
- Scope: Colored blue, values are bug/build/chore/docs/enhancement/feature
- Evaluating: Colored light purple, values are evaluating/"needs bikeshedding"
- No further action: Colored white, values are duplicate/invalid/wontfix
- Don't process immediately: Colored red, values are blocked/breaking/"needs issue"
- Miscellaneous:
  - "accepted" is green
  - "question" is pink

I'm not suggesting that any labels be changed, just their colors for grouping purposes.

issue.title: Shorten commit message length limit to 64 characters

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: Relates to the tools used in the ESLint development process

labels.name: evaluating
labels.description: The team will evaluate this issue to decide whether it meets the criteria for inclusion

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
We currently have a commit message length limit of 72 characters. I suspect this number was chosen because GitHub truncates messages longer than 72 characters and puts them on a new line.

However, since we use GitHub's "squash and merge" feature, the PR number gets appended to the end of a commit message when we merge it, e.g. " (#1234)". This often makes the commit message longer than 72 characters when it gets merged, even though the commit message on the PR was within the length limit on the PR.

" (#1234)" is 8 characters long, so if it's still important to us that commit messages display on one line, we should reduce the length limit to 64 characters to accommodate for the added length. (We would reduce it to 63 characters when we start having five-digit PR IDs.)

Commit messages are also displayed in changelogs and blogposts, so we might also decide that it's worth having the extra space for descriptive messages even if they overflow on GitHub.
